item.title: Best potato harvest in ten years on Hokkaido
item.description: While heat and drought affected crops worldwide this year, Japan's Hokkaido island experienced its best potato harvest in a decade. Hokkaido is virtually the only region in the Northern Hemisphere to see its production increase. Manufacturer Calbee expects to reach the usual 250,000 tons of Hokkaido potatoes. item.title: Parisian women defied trouser ban in 19th century
item.description: In 1800, wearing trousers was banned for women in Paris, intended to keep women out of political life. Yet throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries, many Parisian women continued to break or circumvent this law, dressing and even living as men. item.title: Botero's round figures breathe new life into classical masterpieces
item.description: Colombian artist Fernando Botero reimagined famous European artworks, such as the Mona Lisa, in his distinctive rounded style, known as 'Boterismo'. This style emerged in 1956 when he accidentally painted a hole that was too small in a mandoline, causing the instrument to appear to 'explode' in form and volume. item.description: Gabriela Ponce Santizo, a Guatemalan biologist, has been active in nature conservation for 19 years and is now Country Director of the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) in Guatemala. item.title: Ocean protector Stacy Jupiter fights breast cancer
item.description: Dr. Stacy Jupiter, who coordinates global ocean conservation for the Wildlife Conservation Society, received an unexpected breast cancer diagnosis in September 2025 while on vacation in Florida. There was no visible tumor in her breast, but the cancer had already spread to her lymph nodes. She returned to Boston for treatment, where she underwent a clinical trial, surgery, chemotherapy and...

item.title: NASA SpaceX mission delivers experiments and solar panels to ISS
item.description: NASA's latest SpaceX cargo resupply mission has successfully launched toward the International Space Station (ISS). The flight carries thousands of pounds of supplies, scientific equipment, and new technology to the station. This cargo is intended to support research in Earth orbit. In addition to crew necessities, the mission also includes solar panels for the ISS.

item.description: On October 9, 2026, NASA published a final request for proposals inviting American companies to develop the next generation of commercial space stations. item.description: Two weeks after its launch, the European Copernicus satellite Sentinel-3C has transmitted its first images and measurements to Earth. item.description: Researchers in Europe are gaining easier access to research data and digital services thanks to the launch of the first 13 hubs within the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) Federation. These so-called EOSC Nodes connect research resources from different organizations and help scientists collaborate across borders and disciplines. item.description: Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco have demonstrated for the first time in humans that the psychedelic psilocybin can reduce inflammation markers. In a small pilot study with 12 participants with Parkinson's disease, five inflammatory signaling molecules were measured in the blood before and after two psilocybin sessions. item.title: Crows make decisions twice as fast as humans
item.description: New research published in the journal Science shows that crows convert visual information into decisions at remarkable speed — twice as fast as humans and primates. Researcher Andreas Nieder from the University of Tübingen trained crows to perform a classic test also used in humans and apes: recognizing the direction of moving dots on a screen. item.title: Rare jaguar filmed near Guatemala-Honduras border
item.description: In June, camera traps captured a male jaguar in Guatemala's forest areas, close to the border with Honduras. Conservation organization Panthera calls the footage, which occurs only once every ten years, a milestone for the jaguar species threatened in Guatemala. item.description: At the Waterfowl Sanctuary in Godmanchester, England, Graham Porter received a call from an angler whose fishing line had hooked a young swan. item.title: HART Rescue saves feral cats as farm cats
item.description: In 2015, Jennifer Cabral and Deb Mathews founded HART Rescue in Crossville, Tennessee. Instead of euthanizing feral, semi-feral or unsocialized cats, the organization places them as working farm cats with local farmers. To date, 634 cats have been rehomed this way. item.title: Threatened leopard shark spotted for first time in Samoan waters
item.description: Scientists from National Geographic Pristine Seas have filmed a leopard shark, also known as a zebra shark, in Samoan waters for the first time. The footage was captured using a Baited Remote Underwater Video (BRUV), a camera system placed on the seafloor without divers to document marine life. item.description: Vasikaran, a sloth bear from India nicknamed Vasi, lost his left hind leg in 2019 after it became trapped in a snare. The organization Wildlife SOS rescued him, but veterinarians had to amputate the limb. item.title: Floating wetlands bring nature back to Bristol Harbour
item.description: Climate activists and conservation charity WWT have created floating wetlands along the concrete quays of Bristol Harbour. The platforms, measuring 100 and 16 square metres, are made entirely from recycled, recyclable and biodegradable materials, such as old water pipes and coconut fibres.
